The fairness of allocations resulting from pure Nash equilibria in the Round-Robin mechanism has been reassessed, revealing that not all such allocations are envy-free with respect to true valuations. However, it has been established that every pure Nash equilibrium of fixed recursively balanced picking sequences guarantees a lower bound of $1/2$-EF1 and proportional allocations up to one good.

 - Reevaluation of fairness in Round-Robin Nash equilibria.
 - New guarantees established for recursively balanced picking sequences.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23686

---


Category: Technology
Importance: 5
Recent research in game theory has demonstrated that not all pure Nash equilibria of the Round-Robin mechanism lead to allocations that are envy-free up to one good (EF1). However, every such equilibrium does induce an allocation that is 1/2-EF1 and proportional up to one good (PROP1), along with a specific limitation on guarantees for all equilibria.

 - The research corrects an earlier claim regarding the fairness of pure Nash equilibria in the Round-Robin mechanism.
 - It establishes that while no better guarantee than 2/3-EF1 exists for all equilibria, the proposed mechanisms still retain some fairness properties.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23686
